back: The diagonal of a unit square is $\sqrt2$, and no fraction equals it. Legend says the Greeks who found this were shaken by it.

title: Factor tree
back: Split until every branch is prime. Whichever way you split, the primes at the end are the same.

title: Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic
back: Every composite number is a product of primes in one way only (apart from order). The key word is unique.

title: HCF from prime factors
back: Only the common primes, each with its smallest power.

title: LCM from prime factors
back: Every prime that appears, each with its greatest power.

title: HCF × LCM
back: True for two numbers only, never for three.

title: Proving √p irrational
tex: \begin{gathered}\sqrt p=\tfrac ab\ (\text{coprime})\\ \downarrow\\ pb^2=a^2\Rightarrow p\mid a\\ \downarrow\\ a=pc\Rightarrow p\mid b\\ \downarrow\\ \text{contradiction}\end{gathered}
back: Write 'coprime' in line 1: it is what the last line contradicts.

title: Can it end in 0?
back: A number ends in 0 only if its prime factors include both 2 and 5. $6^n=2^n\cdot3^n$ has no 5.

title: Mixing rational and irrational
back: But irrational × irrational may be rational: $\sqrt2\times\sqrt2=2$.

title: HCF or LCM?
back: Bells, lights and runners meeting again: LCM. Equal groups, biggest tile, longest tape: HCF.
